podcast.body: This 1973 cover of Jerry Lorton's 1960 instrumental became famously known as "The Incredible Bongo Rock" and is often dubbed the "national anthem of hip-hop." The track is characterized by its "crazed piece of orchestral funk" and, most significantly, a minute-long percussion break featuring a trap drummer and congaist dueling. DJ Kool Herk successfully used this break to popularize his "merry go round" technique, leading to its widespread use in early hip-hop. Music writer Michael Angelo Matos highlighted its enduring influence, noting it would be remade and sampled countless times, especially when sampling was less legally regulated. "Everybody is still using Bongo Rock's Apache."
